headline: AMERICAS GOLD & SILVER SURGES 17%: Record 787,000 oz Silver Q1 Plus Six New Galena Complex Veins
snippet: Americas Gold and Silver (TSX: USA / NYSE American: USAS) jumped 17% on May 7 after reporting record Q1 silver production of 787,000 ounces alongside the discovery of six new high-grade veins at the Galena Complex in Idaho — including the 43L-TJ Vein Complex carrying significant silver, copper, and antimony grades.

headline: SILVER47 HITS 38.7 g/t GOLD, 1,713 g/t SILVER at Kennedy: 15 km Untested Nevada Vein Network Mapped
snippet: Silver47 Exploration (TSXV: AGA / OTCQX: AAGAF) released rock sample results from the expanded Kennedy Gold-Silver Project in Nevada on May 7, returning up to 38.7 g/t Au and 1,713 g/t Ag across a 6,150-acre land package with a largely untested 15 km vein network that has seen minimal modern exploration.

headline: MANHATTAN URANIUM DISCOVERY Closes Dual Acquisition, Launches as MANU: 15 Past-Producing U.S. Mines
snippet: The TSX-V company formerly known as Aero Energy completed court-approved acquisitions of Urano Energy and Pegasus Resources on May 7, rebranding as Manhattan Uranium Discovery Corp (TSX-V: MANU) with a 25,099-acre portfolio spanning 15 past-producing uranium mines across 25 U.S. properties — nearly all votes cast were in favour of both deals.

headline: SSR MINING STOCK +20%: Earnings Triple to $1.15/Share as $4,770 Realized Gold Sends Revenue Up 84%
snippet: SSR Mining's Q1 blowout on May 6 sent shares up 20%, with earnings of $1.15 per share nearly tripling year-over-year as the company's average realized gold price surged to $4,770 per ounce and revenue climbed 84% — a textbook illustration of how high gold prices flow directly to mid-tier producer margins.

headline: MP MATERIALS Locks Apple and Pentagon as Customers: U.S.'s Only Fully Integrated Rare Earth Producer
snippet: MP Materials (NYSE: MP), operator of California's Mountain Pass mine and the only fully integrated rare earth producer in the U.S., announced landmark supply agreements with Apple and the Pentagon — deals that cement its strategic position as Washington bets on domestic rare earth independence.

headline: GDX BREAKS KEY RESISTANCE, SURGES 6%: Gold Miners Finally Catching Up to the Metal's Massive Bull Run
snippet: Gold miners (GDX) surged 6.16% on May 6 and broke above the $42–46 resistance zone that had capped the sector, while silver miners (SIL) rallied 6.56% and cleared their own key resistance level — prompting analysts to argue the long-awaited miner catch-up trade to the metal may now be underway.

headline: CHINA BANS SULPHURIC ACID EXPORTS: Iran War Fallout Now Threatens One-Fifth of Chile's Copper Output
snippet: China is halting sulphuric acid exports from May 2026 after the Iran war severed Middle Eastern sulphur supply — and Chile is the first major casualty, with one-fifth of its copper output dependent on acid-leach processing and local acid prices already up 44% in a single month.

headline: CHILE LITHIUM SURGES 175% YOY TO $498M in April While Copper Stalls Under Supply Chain Pressures
snippet: Chile's April 2026 export data shows lithium carbonate revenues soaring 175.6% year-over-year to $498 million, sharply outperforming flat copper figures — a divergence that highlights where battery metals demand is still pulling capital even as base metals face new supply chain headwinds.

headline: STANDARD URANIUM Mobilizes for 10,000m Athabasca Basin Drill: Same Structural Trend as NexGen Arrow
snippet: Standard Uranium (TSX-V: STND / OTCQB: STTDF) has finalized targets and is mobilizing for a fully-funded 8,000–10,000m drill program at its flagship Davidson River project in Saskatchewan's southwest Athabasca Basin, with two rigs targeting the Warrior, Bronco, and Thunderbird corridors on the same structural trend that hosts NexGen Energy's Arrow and Paladin Energy's Triple R deposits.

headline: SILVER TOPS $79, UP 150% IN A YEAR: Analysts Say Historic Precious Metals Rally Set to Resume as Fog Lifts
snippet: Silver climbed above $79 an ounce this week — up more than 150% over the past year — while gold held near $4,700 after pulling back from Q1 highs above $5,500. Market watchers say both metals' secular bull runs are intact and could resume strongly once the geopolitical 'fog of war' around the U.S.-Iran situation clarifies.

headline: THE PAPER DIVERGENCE: Western Gold Futures and Physical Bullion Markets Are Splitting — and It Matters
snippet: A May 5 analysis published by Money Metals highlights the widening gap between paper-traded gold and silver on Western futures exchanges versus the physical bullion market, arguing this structural divergence — driven by delivery bottlenecks and changing institutional demand — is a meaningful signal that most retail investors are not watching.

headline: Junior Mining Exploration Hits $6.2B But GRASSROOTS Spending Falls to Record Low 21%: The Discovery Deficit
snippet: Global mining exploration budgets climbed 11% to $6.2 billion in 2025, yet the share going toward genuine grassroots discovery programs collapsed to a record low of just 21% — meaning the industry is spending more than ever on mining while funding less of the early-stage work that produces tomorrow's deposits.
